lyrics:
[Intro: waltz-time piano, harmonica melody, bar noise]

[Verse 1: warm storyteller, piano and accordion]
The leagues have gone home with their trophies
The lanes have gone dark for the night
There's a man in a bowling shirt signing up twice
For a song that he never gets right

[Verse 2: bass and brushed drums join]
There's Marge who sells life insurance
She sings like a kettle in love
And Darnell from the night shift does opera in Spanish
With a dish towel for a glove

[Chorus: whole bar singing, glasses clinking]
So sing it for us, it's your turn
Nobody here can sing
We came for the chorus, we stay for each other
And nobody's judging a thing
La, la-la, di-da-da
La-la, di-da-da, da-dum

[Harmonica Break: harmonica and accordion in waltz time]

[Verse 3: storyteller, a little softer]
The twins at the back do a duet
In keys that have yet to be named
And the widow from Tuesday's has dedicated one
To a man she has never once blamed

[Verse 4: storyteller, about himself]
And I run the machine and I hold out the mic
I was going to be someone, I thought
But I've heard every heart in this town through a speaker
And it's better than what I'd have bought

[Chorus: whole bar singing, louder]
So sing it for us, it's your turn
Nobody here can sing
We came for the chorus, we stay for each other
And nobody's judging a thing
La, la-la, di-da-da
La-la, di-da-da, da-dum

[Outro: piano and harmonica slow down, last call bell, applause]
Who's next?
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: A slow waltz, three beats to the bar at about 60 bars a minute, in C major. Swaying, warm and a little wistful.

VOICE: Male, warm and conversational, a storyteller's tenor with clear words and a smile in it. The chorus is sung by a whole bar of people, off-key in places, with clinking glasses and a few shouts, and a wordless 'la-la' tag.

INSTRUMENTS: An upright piano playing a rolling waltz figure. A harmonica playing the tune between verses. An accordion. Upright bass. Brushed drums with a soft waltz pattern. A mandolin in the last verse. Bar ambience, a bell and applause.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, piano and harmonica over bar noise. 0:20 Verse 1. 0:44 Verse 2. 1:08 Chorus 1, the bar sings. 1:38 Harmonica break. 1:58 Verse 3. 2:22 Verse 4, the host about himself. 2:46 Chorus 2, louder. 3:16 The 'la-la' tag repeats with the crowd. 3:50 Outro, the band slows, a last-orders bell, applause and two spoken words at 4:20.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-1970s singer-songwriter recording made to feel live: warm piano, close voice, the crowd recorded as a room.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The first chorus, when the bar comes in.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: Verse 4 is the change. The original narrator is passing through and knows he is better than the room. This one stayed, and has decided that hearing every heart in town through a speaker beats the career he imagined.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Fond observation, tenderness, contentment.
